To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 404- and 915-MHz wind profilers and the 50-MHz RASS system provided accurate and useful measurements of the atmospheric state during the winter of 1991 in Colorado.
the 50-MHz wind profilers and RASSs were able to measure the wind and virtual temperature profiles to the lowest altitudes and the 404-MHz wind profiler was able to measure the highest altitudes.
(a) the 404- and 915-MHz wind profilers performed well, and (b) the 50-MHz wind profiler and the 404-MHz RASS performed well, but (c) the 915-MHz RASS did not perform well.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of remote-sensor systems for the measurement of wind and temperature.
the development of a new technology for the measurement of atmospheric winds and temperatures from a ground-based platform.
the evaluation and development of remote sensing systems that can be used for atmospheric measurements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the wind profilers are a mature technology and are ready to be used in operational weather prediction and climate studies.
wind profilers are an extremely useful tool for atmospheric research, particularly in the lower troposphere.
the wind-profiling radars and the microwave radiometer performed as advertised and that they can be expected to provide reliable data for a wide variety of meteorological applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the remote-sensing systems performed well.
the remote sensing of winds, water vapor, and liquid water is now feasible with a level of accuracy and precision comparable to that obtained with in situ instruments.
the remote sensors performed as well or better than expected.
The main takeaway from our work is that
wind profiler and RASS technology is ready for operational use in many applications.
the 404-MHz WPDN system is a good performer.

the 50- and 404-MHz wind profilers, along with RASS, are very effective in measuring the vertical structure of the atmosphere, especially when used in conjunction with microwave radiometers for profiling water vapor.
